title: PAR-06: Store.reconstructBounded() in src/event_store/store.zig is dead code -- unused duplicate of reconstruction.zig's live bounded-reconstruction path, risk of future behavioral drift
summary: src/event_store/store.zig's Store.reconstructBounded() (PAR-06, commit 9ac7c2eb) is not called anywhere in src/ or tests/ -- confirmed via grep, which only matches its own definition/doc comments and one test-file comment describing it. The live PAR-06 bounded-reconstruction path is src/engine/reconstruction.zig's eventWindowForInstanceInTx() + reconstructInstance(), an independently-written duplicate of the same window-lookup-and-repair logic. The two disagree on tenant scoping: Store.reconstructBounded() takes an explicit tenant_id parameter and filters events/events_archive by it; reconstruction.zig's live path has no tenant_id parameter or predicate anywhere, relying entirely on search_path scoping, which is correct for the current schema since instance_projections had its tenant_id column dropped by GBL-084/GBL-123_rls_removal.sql (events/events_archive still carry tenant_id today, re-added by PAR-01/migration 1147, so Store.reconstructBounded()'s query is schema-valid, just unreachable). Not an active vulnerability since the dead function isn't called, but a maintenance hazard: a future caller could wire up the more 'defensively scoped'-looking dead function without realizing reconstruction.zig's version is the actually-integrated one, producing inconsistent tenant-scoping behavior between two code paths meant to do the same thing.

root_cause.details: PAR-06's design doc left the exact call-site ambiguous ('whether exposed as a new Store.reconstructBounded() wrapper, or a function inside reconstruction.zig that itself performs the lookup' -- design doc Open questions). BACKEND-DEV implemented both instead of choosing one, leaving Store.reconstructBounded() as unreferenced dead code alongside the actually-wired reconstruction.zig implementation.

independent_verification.zero_live_callers: Confirmed via `grep -rn "reconstructBounded" src/ tests/`: only matches are the definition itself (store.zig:1259), its own doc comments (store.zig:1234/1713), one unrelated comment in src/engine/instance.zig:83 describing a numeric convention it shares, the PAR-06 design doc (src/design/par-06-time-bounded-reconstruction.md:78,196,301), and test-file comments in tests/integration/par06_reconstruction_bounded_test.zig and tests/specs/PAR-06.md that explicitly document it as dead. Zero actual call expressions anywhere in src/ or tests/.
independent_verification.test_file_header_confirms: tests/integration/par06_reconstruction_bounded_test.zig lines 6-12 state outright: 'Store.reconstructBounded() is DEAD CODE -- not called anywhere in src/ or tests/. The actually-wired PAR-06 reconstruction entry point is src/engine/reconstruction.zig's reconstructInstance(). Every test below exercises that live path, not the unreferenced Store.reconstructBounded().' The test suite has already converged on reconstruction.zig as sole source of truth.
independent_verification.tenant_scoping_divergence: Confirmed by reading both implementations in full. Store.reconstructBounded() (store.zig:1259-1353) takes an explicit tenant_id parameter and adds `AND tenant_id = $4::uuid` to both its events and events_archive queries (store.zig:1294, 1323). reconstruction.zig's live reconstructInstance() -> eventWindowForInstanceInTx() (reconstruction.zig:87-260, 1277-1379) has no tenant_id parameter or predicate anywhere in its instance_projections lookup or its events/events_archive UNION ALL query (reconstruction.zig:122-128, 170-191) -- relies entirely on search_path scoping. The live path's approach is schema-correct: instance_projections lost its tenant_id column via GBL-084/GBL-123_rls_removal.sql, so a tenant_id predicate against it (as the dead lookupOrRepairEventWindowInternal() does at store.zig:1372-1379, which queries instance_projections WITHOUT a tenant_id filter despite Store.reconstructBounded() itself taking a tenant_id param) would not even be exercised consistently -- the dead code's own internal helper never applies tenant scoping to the instance_projections lookup, only to the later events/events_archive queries. events/events_archive still carry tenant_id (PAR-01/migration 1147), so the dead function's events-table queries are schema-valid but simply unreachable.
independent_verification.empty_window_divergence: Confirmed. store.zig's lookupOrRepairEventWindowInternal() (store.zig:1361-1457): when the repair scan (MIN/MAX(created_at) over events WHERE instance_id=$1) finds zero rows, it returns StoreError.ReconstructionWindowMissing (store.zig:1415, 1450) -- a hard error. reconstruction.zig's eventWindowForInstanceInTx() (reconstruction.zig:1277-1379): when the identical repair scan finds zero rows, it does NOT error -- it falls back to an unbounded-in-effect window [0, now+1] (reconstruction.zig:1316-1338), with an explicit comment explaining why: 'the instance's rows may have already fully migrated to events_archive... a bounded query that finds zero rows here would incorrectly report InstanceNotFound for a real, fully-archived instance.' This is a genuine behavioral divergence, not just a naming difference -- the dead code's error-on-empty-scan behavior would incorrectly fail reconstruction for exactly the fully-archived-instance case the live code explicitly handles.
independent_verification.reachability_of_error_variants: StoreError.ReconstructionWindowMissing (store.zig:87) is returned ONLY by the dead lookupOrRepairEventWindowInternal() (2 return sites, store.zig:1415 and 1450) -- grep across the whole repo confirms no other production code path constructs it. StoreError.UnboundedReconstructionRefused (store.zig:93) is declared but never constructed/returned anywhere in src/ -- confirmed vestigial (only referenced in comments at store.zig:1284/1286 and the design doc). Neither variant appears in any switch-on-StoreError elsewhere in the codebase: the only function that switches on StoreError, retentionPolicyErrorCode() (store.zig:1737-1743), uses a catch-all `else => null` arm, so it is non-exhaustive and compiles unaffected regardless of which StoreError variants exist. No other file in src/ contains a `switch (err)` matching these two variant names by identifier.
independent_verification.recommendation: Option 1 -- delete Store.reconstructBounded() and its private helpers (lookupOrRepairEventWindowInternal, mergeEventRowsBySequence, rowSequenceNumber) from store.zig, and delete the now-fully-unreachable StoreError.ReconstructionWindowMissing and StoreError.UnboundedReconstructionRefused variants (with their doc comments, store.zig:81-93) since deleting reconstructBounded() removes their only producers/references and no switch statement in the codebase requires their continued existence (retentionPolicyErrorCode()'s switch has an else catch-all). reconstruction.zig remains the single, already-tested, already-correct (for the current post-GBL-084/GBL-123 schema) source of truth for PAR-06 bounded reconstruction. Option 2 (wiring reconstruction.zig to delegate to Store.reconstructBounded()) is NOT recommended: it would require reconstruction.zig to either (a) drop its correct empty-window fallback behavior to match the dead code's incorrect ReconstructionWindowMissing-on-empty-scan behavior, silently breaking fully-archived-instance reconstruction, or (b) keep two divergent behaviors reconciled through extra glue code, which is strictly more complexity than deleting the unused duplicate. There is no evidence of a future non-reconstruction.zig caller that would need Store.reconstructBounded() as a public API -- the design doc's Open Questions #1 left this genuinely undecided at design time, but empirical evidence (test suite convergence, zero call sites, live code's schema-correctness) now resolves it in favor of reconstruction.zig being THE entry point.

resolution: Deleted Store.reconstructBounded() and its three private helpers (lookupOrRepairEventWindowInternal, mergeEventRowsBySequence, rowSequenceNumber) from src/event_store/store.zig, per ISSUE-FIXER/CODE-DESIGNER's independently-confirmed recommendation (option 1: delete, not delegate). Also deleted the two StoreError variants that became fully unreachable once the dead helper was gone (ReconstructionWindowMissing -- previously reachable only from the deleted helper's two return sites; UnboundedReconstructionRefused -- already vestigial, never constructed anywhere) along with their doc comments, and the now-unused EventWindow struct (grep confirmed zero remaining references after the function deletions). src/engine/reconstruction.zig's reconstructInstance()/eventWindowForInstanceInTx() is confirmed as the sole live PAR-06 bounded-reconstruction path going forward; no behavioral change was made to that file. Cleaned up stale references to the deleted function: src/engine/instance.zig:83's comment reworded to cite reconstruction.zig's eventWindowForInstanceInTx()/reconstructInstance() instead of the deleted function by name; src/design/par-06-time-bounded-reconstruction.md got a new 'Resolution (GH-716)' section appended after its historical Open Questions (which were left unchanged as the accurate historical record); tests/integration/par06_reconstruction_bounded_test.zig's file header and tests/specs/PAR-06.md's implementation note were updated from present-tense 'is DEAD CODE' to past-tense 'was dead code ... removed (GH-716)'; tests/integration/par06_instance_projections_event_window_test.zig's header comment (a third stale reference found during verification, not in the original file list) was also updated -- it asserted schema-slice-only tests were exercised via 'store.zig's own reconstructBounded()/append() call paths', which is no longer true now that function is gone; reworded to point at reconstruction.zig instead.
verification: zig build: exit 0, compiles clean. zig build check (PI-03 gate: build + scoped `zig fmt --check` against the 4 changed .zig files): PASSED after running `zig fmt` on all 4 changed files. python tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests: 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, 0 MINOR. zig build test-integration-par06 (against real PostgreSQL via BPM_TEST_DB_URL, port 5434 per .env): 3/3 tests passed. zig build test-integration-par06-reconstruction (same real PostgreSQL): 5/5 tests passed -- both were expected to be unaffected since they already exercised only the live reconstruction.zig path, and this confirms it. Full unit suite (zig build test): Build Summary 103/103 steps succeeded; 1071/1135 tests passed (64 skipped, pre-existing baseline unrelated to this change) -- no regressions, exit 0.
prevention: Delete Store.reconstructBounded() and its private helpers (lookupOrRepairEventWindowInternal, mergeEventRowsBySequence, rowSequenceNumber) from store.zig, leaving reconstruction.zig as the single source of truth for PAR-06 bounded reconstruction -- OR wire reconstruction.zig to delegate to Store.reconstructBounded() if that is meant to be the long-term public API.
Either way, end up with exactly one implementation of the window-lookup-and-repair logic, not two independently maintained copies that can drift on tenant-scoping behavior.
